title: Lifting geometric specializations to strict local schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $t,s\in S$ satisfy $s\in\overline{\{t\}}$, and choose geometric points $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_t\to S$ and $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_s\to S$ over $t,s$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. For the strict local scheme $S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] with structural map $p:S_{(\bar s)}\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], there exists a morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_t\to S_{(\bar s)}$ satisfying $p\circ a=\bar t$.

proof.text: Apply strictHenselizationResidue, using the residue-field embedding determined by the geometric point, to give H its local-ring structure and identify the image of its closed point with s. Choose an affine open chart i:Spec R→S containing s. Every point of Spec H generalizes its closed point; continuity and stability of open subsets under generalization show that the entire structural map p factors through i. The factorization g is IsOpenImmersion.lift, and Spec full faithfulness supplies its ring map b:R→H.

Apply strictHenselization_indEtale_of_affine_chart to b, the identity identification of Spec H with the strict local scheme, and the factorization g≫i=p. Thus H is ind-etale over R. The existing Algebra.IndEtale.weaklyEtale instance makes b weakly etale, and weaklyEtale_SpecMap_algebraMap makes g weakly etale. The open immersion i is weakly etale; stability under composition therefore makes p weakly etale, hence flat.

Since t specializes to s=p(closedPoint H), apply Flat.generalizingMap to p and the closed point. It yields x in Spec H with p(x)=t. Apply Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback to x and the unique point of Spec Ωt to obtain a point v of the pullback of p along the prescribed barT; their images agree by hbarT.

The projection q from this pullback to Spec Ωt is weakly etale by base change. Apply exists_comp_eq_id_of_weaklyEtale to q and v, obtaining a section σ. Define a as σ followed by the other pullback projection. Associativity, the pullback commutativity equation and σ≫q=id give a≫p=barT. No choices of geometric embeddings or residue-field identifications are needed in this final combination.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GJ5, remark-can-lift, shortened using the existing strict-henselization affine-chart ind-etale theorem, Tag 03HV generalization lifting for flat morphisms, and the existing algebraically closed weakly-etale section theorem (Tag 0F6C proof). X9, 2026-10-18.
